The [[1912 Summer Olympics]], officially known as the Games of the V Olympiad, were an international [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Stockholm]], Sweden, between 5 May and 27 July 1912.<ref>{{cite web |title=FAQ: What are the Olympic Games? |url=https://olympic.ca/2019/02/08/faq-what-are-the-olympic-games/ |website=[[Canadian Olympic Committee]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |date=8 February 2019 |archive-date=20 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250220175124/https://olympic.ca/2019/02/08/faq-what-are-the-olympic-games/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="1912 Olympedia">{{cite web |title=1912 Summer Olympics Overview |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/6 |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=14 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250214133446/https://www.olympedia.org/editions/6 |url-status=live }}</ref> A total of 2,407 athletes representing 28 National Olympic Committees (NOCs) participated,<ref>{{cite web |title=Stockholm 1912 Summer Olympics – Athletes, Medals & Results |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/stockholm-1912 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=26 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240926064855/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/stockholm-1912 |url-status=live }}</ref> which included seven teams making their Olympic debut at the Summer Games; [[Chile at the 1912 Summer Olympics|Chile]],<ref name="Chile IOC">{{cite web |title=Chile – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/chile |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006042622/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/chile |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=2024-12-30 }}</ref> [[Egypt at the 1912 Summer Olympics|Egypt]],<ref name="Egypt IOC">{{cite web |title=Egypt – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/egypt |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006042915/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/egypt |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=2024-12-30 }}</ref> [[Iceland at the 1912 Summer Olympics|Iceland]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Iceland (ISL) |url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/ISL |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=6 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231006202147/http://www.olympedia.org/countries/ISL |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Japan at the 1912 Summer Olympics|Japan]],<ref name="Japan IOC">{{cite web |title=Japan – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/japan |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006043509/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/luxembourg |archive-date=2024-10-06 |url-status=dead |access-date=2024-12-30}}</ref> }}</ref> and [[Serbia at the 1912 Summer Olympics|Serbia]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Serbia (SRB) |url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/SRB |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=3 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003062406/https://www.olympedia.org/countries/SRB |url-status=live }}</ref> The games featured 107 events in 19 disciplines.<ref name="1912 Olympedia" /> The games included the Olympic debut of equestrian dressage and eventing, as well as the modern pentathlon.<ref>{{cite web |title=Equestrian Sport: History of Equestrian Sport at the Olympic Games |url=https://stillmed.olympic.org/media/Document%20Library/OlympicOrg/Factsheets-Reference-Documents/Games/OG/History-of-sports/Reference-document-Equestrian-Sport-History-at-the-OG.pdf |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |page=3 |date=October 19, 2017 |archive-date=28 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728022839/https://stillmed.olympic.org/media/Document%20Library/OlympicOrg/Factsheets-Reference-Documents/Games/OG/History-of-sports/Reference-document-Equestrian-Sport-History-at-the-OG.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Modern Pentathlon: Olympic history, rules, latest updates and upcoming events for the Olympic sport |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/sports/modern-pentathlon/ |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=23 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123075139/https://www.olympics.com/en/sports/modern-pentathlon/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Athletes representing 19 NOCs received at least one medal, with 16 winning at least one gold medal.<ref name="IOC medal table" /> [[Sweden at the 1912 Summer Olympics|Sweden]] won the most medals overall, with 65, while the [[United States at the 1912 Summer Olympics|United States]] won the most gold medals, with 44.<ref name="IOC medal table" /> Among individual participants, Swedish shooter [[Vilhelm Carlberg]], Finnish runner [[Hannes Kolehmainen]], and American shooter [[Alfred Lane]] tied for the most gold medals, with three each.<ref name="SR">{{cite web |title=1912 Stockholm Summer Games |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1912/ |website=[[Sports Reference]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417041204/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1912/ |archive-date=April 17, 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Carlberg had the most total medals, with five (three gold, two silver).<ref name="SR" />

==Medal table==
[[File:Jim Thorpe 1912b.jpg|thumb|right|alt=Jim Thorpe standing with his hands on his side in shorts and an Olympic T-shirt.|American athlete [[Jim Thorpe]] won gold medals in the [[Athletics at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's pentathlon|men's pentathlon]] and [[Athletics at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's decathlon|decathlon]] events. His gold medals were stripped after he was found to have previously been a paid athlete. He was re-awarded the medals in 1982, as co-winner, and declared the sole winner of the events in 2022 by the IOC.<ref name="Thorpe2">{{cite news |title=Jim Thorpe Is Restored as Sole Winner of 1912 Olympic Gold Medals |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/07/15/sports/olympics/jim-thorpe-olympics-medal-restored.html |date=2022-07-15 |work=[[The New York Times]] |last1=Mather |first1=Victor |last2=Panja |first2=Tariq |access-date=15 July 2022 |at=sec. B, p. 10 |archive-date=15 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220715150927/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/07/15/sports/olympics/jim-thorpe-olympics-medal-restored.html |url-status=live }}</ref>]]

The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |website=[[The Independent]] | date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=12 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |website=[[The New York Times]] | date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] |date=10 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us }}</ref>

The 1912 Games featured five [[Art competitions at the 1912 Summer Olympics|art competitions]] which awarded medals, but did not do so for a full top three, instead opting to award only a first or first and second place medal. Only gold and no silver or bronze medals were awarded in architecture, literature, music, and painting.<ref name="Olympedia arts">{{cite web |title=Art Competitions at the 1912 Summer Olympics |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/6/sports/ART |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=28 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241228182239/https://www.olympedia.org/editions/6/sports/ART |url-status=live }}</ref> In sculpturing, a gold and silver medal, but no bronze, were awarded.<ref name="Olympedia arts"/>

In the [[Wrestling at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's Greco-Roman light heavyweight|men's light heavyweight Greco-Roman]], the final round featured three wrestlers, [[Anders Ahlgren]], [[Ivar Böhling]], and [[Béla Varga (wrestler)|Béla Varga]], who took turns facing off against one another. Ahlgren and Böhling defeated Varga, but they were unable to defeat each other. The match between Ahlgren and Böhling lasted for over 9 hours without a victor. The Olympic rules at the time specifically stated that the winner must have beaten their opponent, and since neither person could claim to have done so, both Ahlgreen and Böhling were awarded silver medals, with no gold being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Inseparable Ahlgren and Bohling share wrestling gold |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/inseparable-ahlgren-and-bohling-share-wrestling-gold |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=16 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816025812/https://olympics.com/en/news/inseparable-ahlgren-and-bohling-share-wrestling-gold |url-status=live }}</ref>

In [[Rowing at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's single sculls|men's single sculls]] and [[Rowing at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's coxed four|men's coxed four]], there were two-way ties for third which resulted in two bronze medals being awarded in each event.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stockholm 1912 single sculls 1x men Results – Olympic rowing |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/stockholm-1912/results/rowing/single-sculls-1x-men |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=9 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009092628/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/stockholm-1912/results/rowing/single-sculls-1x-men |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Stockholm 1912 four-oared shell with coxswain men Results – Olympic rowing |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/stockholm-1912/results/rowing/four-oared-shell-with-coxswain-men |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=9 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009092625/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/stockholm-1912/results/rowing/four-oared-shell-with-coxswain-men |url-status=live }}</ref> In [[Athletics at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's pole vault|men's pole vault]], there was a two-way tie for second, which resulted in two silver medals being awarded. Additionally, there was a three-way tie for fourth, which the IOC awarded bronze medals for.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stockholm 1912 pole vault men Results – Olympic athletics |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/stockholm-1912/results/athletics/pole-vault-men |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=9 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009092646/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/stockholm-1912/results/athletics/pole-vault-men |url-status=live }}</ref> 

In the [[Tug of war at the 1912 Summer Olympics|tug of war]], three of the five teams withdrew for unknown reasons, resulting in only two teams participating and a bronze medal not being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tug-Of-War at the 1912 Summer Olympics |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/6/sports/TOW |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=20 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120034407/https://www.olympedia.org/editions/6/sports/TOW |url-status=live }}</ref> Three teams made the final round of the [[Athletics at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's 4 × 100 metres relay|men's 4 x 100 metres relay]], but when Germany was disqualified for a faulty baton pass, it resulted in no bronze medal being awarded for the event.<ref>{{cite web |title=4 x 100 metres Relay, Men |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/56677 |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=10 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210110041117/https://www.olympedia.org/results/56677 |url-status=live }}</ref>

| rowspan="8" style="text-align:left;" | [[Jim Thorpe]], the winner of the [[Athletics at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's pentathlon|pentathlon]] and [[Athletics at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's decathlon|decathlon]] events, was subsequently disqualified after having taken expense money for playing semi-professional [[baseball]]. Only amateur athletes were allowed to compete at the time, and by taking money, he was no longer considered an amateur. The athletes ranking second through fourth were upgraded to first through third.<ref name="Thorpe 1">{{cite web |title=IOC reinstates Jim Thorpe as sole winner of 1912 Olympic decathlon and pentathlon |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/34245374/ioc-reinstates-jim-thorpe-sole-winner-1912-olympic-decathlon-pentathlon |website=[[ESPN]] |date=2022-07-14 |last1=Schaap |first1=Jeremy |access-date=15 July 2022 |language=en |archive-date=15 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220715150933/https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/34245374/ioc-reinstates-jim-thorpe-sole-winner-1912-olympic-decathlon-pentathlon |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Thorpe2" />

[[Hugo Wieslander]] had refused to accept the gold medal, being of the opinion that Thorpe was the legitimate gold medallist.<ref name="IOC Thorpe">{{cite web |title=IOC to display the name of Jim Thorpe as sole Stockholm 1912 pentathlon and decathlon gold medallist |url=https://www.olympics.com/ioc/news/ioc-to-display-the-name-of-jim-thorpe-as-sole-stockholm-1912-pentathlon-and-decathlon-gold-medallist |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |date=2022-07-15 |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=16 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816070946/https://olympics.com/ioc/news/ioc-to-display-the-name-of-jim-thorpe-as-sole-stockholm-1912-pentathlon-and-decathlon-gold-medallist |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Ferdinand Bie]] is also thought to have never accepted the gold medal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Campaign launched to recognise Thorpe as sole champion from Stockholm 1912 |url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1096326/stockholm-campaign-thorpe-golds |website=[[Inside the Games]] |date=2020-07-15 |last1=Baker |first1=Philip |access-date=24 February 2025 |archive-date=15 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200715171817/https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1096326/stockholm-campaign-thorpe-golds |url-status=live }}</ref>
